intent: E1+E2 (Grok critiques: 'recall is weak / paraphrase is the common case' and 'zero evidence of effect'). Convert opinion into MEASURED numbers: build an honest 16-case eval corpus of agent-style leaks (benign in-purpose, literal out-of-purpose, digit-normalized, and the documented-gap vectors: base64/hex/word-split/zero-width/value-split/paraphrase), run the REAL gate() over it, and report recall, false-positive rate, per-scope and per-category breakdown, plus gate() latency over N=10000 runs. Honesty absolute: a near-zero known-gap recall is stated as the finding, not hidden.
riskRationale: This receipt measures a SECURITY BOUNDARY's coverage. An over-stated recall number is worse than none, so the measurement itself is graded high risk: the in-scope vs known-gap split exists precisely so the claim cannot be inflated by aggregation.

constraints.detail: 16 cases: 4 benign (literal in-purpose, lookup->answer, non-private, order-id-not-card), 6 in_scope leaks (literal email/card/ssn/unknown-sink, digit-normalized phone/card), 6 known_gap leaks (base64, hex, word-split, zero-width, value-split-across-sinks, light-paraphrase).

OVERALL recall = 6/12 = 50.0% (the corpus is deliberately half known-gap). Reported split: in_scope recall = 6/6 = 100.0%; known_gap recall = 0/6 = 0.0%. The 0% on encoding/split/paraphrase IS the finding, stated plainly.
0/4 benign cases flagged = 0.0% FP rate. Notably the Luhn-invalid 16-digit order id is NOT mistaken for a payment_card.
gate() is a pure fn; over N=10000 warmed runs on a representative leak input: avg 0.35us, median 0.209us, p95 1.083us. Microsecond-scale; effectively free to call pre-ship.

The runner's JSON summary and this receipt carry only ids, scopes, verdicts and aggregate counts — no raw fixture values. Corpus fixtures are synthetic (example.invalid, 555-01xx, 4111 Visa test PAN).
bun test remains green after adding eval/ (eval is not a test file; gate/policy unchanged).

observations.detail: Recall is reported per-scope so aggregation cannot inflate the claim: in_scope 100%, known_gap 0%, overall 50%.
Latency p95 ~1us means the gate adds no meaningful cost to a tool-calling loop's pre-ship step.

Paraphrase/encoding recall is 0%. This confirms Grok's E1 critique as a MEASURED limit, not an opinion. It is the red-before-green target for any future canonicalization round (would flip known_gap cases to leak).

actions.detail: eval/corpus.ts — 16 labeled cases (scope: benign|in_scope|known_gap, truthLeak ground truth).
bun eval/run.ts — real gate() over every case + N=10000 latency loop.
actions.result: recall 50% overall / 100% in_scope / 0% known_gap; FP 0%; latency avg 0.35us median 0.209us p95 1.083us

actions.detail: bun test (regression check after adding eval/).

evidence.note: Redaction-safe aggregate from the runner. Observed numbers only — separated from projection below.

mechanisms: A stated, measured coverage envelope: the gate catches literal + digit-normalized out-of-purpose leaks at 100% recall with 0% FP and microsecond latency, and openly misses encoded/split/paraphrased leaks (0% recall on those vectors today).
The corpus + runner are a reusable harness: any future canonicalizer can be measured against the same 16 cases, and the known_gap rows are the red-before-green targets.
projection.notes: Context only, not a score. Numbers are from hand-built GateInput fixtures, NOT a live agent wire. The 0% known-gap recall is a verified-disproved win per 0.0.1: the limit is now a measured fact, not an unstated risk. Latency is machine-specific (single dev run); the order of magnitude (sub-microsecond) is the takeaway, not the exact digits.
